newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures rose for the third day in a row on Wednesday due to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 22,710 yuan ($2,737) per tonne, rising 130 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 22,800 and hit a low of 22,560.
March rose 110 to 22,420, April 80 to 22,590, June 150 to 22,710 and July 140 to 22,690.
Combined volume fell sharply to 38,010 tonnes from 103,530.
Copper opened higher on overnight LME gains, but profit-taking pushed prices down from highs for most of the session, traders said.
"Speculative buying pushed the prices up early in the session but few investors were willing to build fresh long positions at such a high level," one trader said.
"Many long position holders preferred to liquidate part of their positions at these levels for profit," he added.
"Investors began to be concerned about possible corrections after the heavy gains of the past few sessions," a second trader said. "But the price is unlikely to fall sharply."
Analysts said they expect Shanghai copper to consolidate at high levels if it can continue to match the strong trends of the LME.
Aluminium ended down. March fell 150 to 15,410 yuan per tonne, May 100 to 15,750 and June 40 to 15,910.
Combined volume rose to 1,720 tonnes from 1,290.
